results.question: What was the company-wide DSO on invoices raised in FY26 (April 2025 to March 2026)?
results.answer_text: No defined DSO metric covered this, so I used ad hoc SQL. Across the 12,239 FY26 invoices (₹4.89bn), the invoice-value-weighted average time from invoice to full payment was about 39.8 days. Every one of these invoices is now fully paid, so a balance-based DSO (open receivables ÷ invoiced × 365) comes out at 0 and isn't useful. The simple unweighted average was about 50.9 days.

results.question: How many days of stock did the channel hold overall, across all distributors and SKUs, in the week of Monday 14 September 2026?
results.answer_text: In the week of 14 Sep 2026 (snapshot 20 Sep), the channel held about 69.4 days of stock overall. That is 2,471,122 units on hand divided by about 35,621 units of average daily secondary sales, summed across 6,246 distributor-SKU rows. A simple average of the per-row days-of-stock figures gives a lower 57.4. The week is not yet settled, so late secondary reporting could change the figure. No defined metric covered this, so I used ad-hoc SQL.

results.question: Which five distributors had the highest DSO on invoices raised in FY26?
results.answer_text: No defined DSO metric covered this, so I used ad-hoc SQL. All FY26 invoices (Apr 2025–Mar 2026) are fully paid, so a balance-based DSO is 0 for every distributor. I ranked instead by invoice-value-weighted days from invoice to final payment. The top five are Mishra Agencies (D0019) at 81.5 days, Rina Pradhan Sales Corporation (D0004) at 79.2, Paul Traders (D0133) at 78.4, Amit Sarkar & Sons (D0199) at 78.2 and Green Valley Marketing (D0129) at 76.7.
sql: SELECT * FROM (SELECT i.distributor_id, d.distributor_name, COUNT(*) AS invoices, ROUND(CAST((SUM((COALESCE(fully_paid_date, last_payment_date) - invoice_date) * invoice_amount_inr) / SUM(invoice_amount_inr)) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS wtd_days_to_pay, SUM(open_amount_inr) AS open_inr FROM marts.fct_invoice_collections AS i JOIN marts.dim_distributor AS d USING (distributor_id) WHERE invoice_date BETWEEN '2025-04-01' AND '2026-03-31' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 4 DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 5) AS q LIMIT 500

If you meant a different definition, such as DSO or on-time share of due invoices, tell me and I'll rerun it.

results.question: For tanks manufactured in FY26, what was the warranty registration rate at each plant?
results.answer_text: For tanks made in FY26 (1 Apr 2025 to 31 Mar 2026), the warranty registration rate within 90 days of shipment was 67.2% at Durgapur, 66.9% at Guwahati and 64.7% at Howrah. results.question: By region, how did the channel stock-out rate over the 13 weeks from 29 December 2025 to 29 March 2026 compare with the 13 weeks from 22 June to 20 September 2026?
results.answer_text: Stock-out rates fell in every region between the two 13-week windows (29 Dec 2025–29 Mar 2026 vs 22 Jun–20 Sep 2026). The rate is the share of distributor-SKU-days in stock-out. No governed metric covered this, so I used ad-hoc SQL. Rates, earlier then later: Assam 2.75% to 2.32%; Bihar & Jharkhand 3.33% to 2.39%; North Bengal & Sikkim 3.70% to 2.40%; North East 3.42% to 2.37%; Odisha 3.02% to 2.24%; South Bengal 3.08% to 2.35%. North Bengal & Sikkim improved the most, and Assam the least.
results.confidence_note: 16/17 figures traced to query results; untraced: 13.

results.question: How did the cost of warranty claims filed in FY26 compare with those filed in FY25?

results.question: By sales region, how did DSO on invoices raised in FY26 compare with FY25?
results.answer_text: No defined metric covered this, so I used ad hoc SQL. I measured DSO as the invoice-value-weighted average days from invoice date to full payment, for invoices raised in each fiscal year (FY26 is Apr 2025–Mar 2026). DSO was essentially flat in every region (FY25 → FY26, in days): Assam 39.6 → 40.0, Bihar & Jharkhand 38.2 → 38.9, North Bengal & Sikkim 42.3 → 42.1, North East 42.8 → 42.9, Odisha 39.6 → 39.6, South Bengal 38.2 → 38.2. All FY25 and FY26 invoices are fully paid, so these figures are complete.
sql: SELECT * FROM (SELECT region, MAX(CASE WHEN fy = 'FY25' THEN d END) AS fy25, MAX(CASE WHEN fy = 'FY26' THEN d END) AS fy26, MAX(CASE WHEN fy = 'FY26' THEN d END) - MAX(CASE WHEN fy = 'FY25' THEN d END) AS change_days FROM (SELECT i.region, d.fiscal_year_label AS fy, ROUND(CAST((SUM((i.fully_paid_date - i.invoice_date) * i.invoice_amount_inr) / SUM(i.invoice_amount_inr)) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS d FROM marts.fct_invoice_collections AS i JOIN marts.dim_date AS d ON d.date_day = i.invoice_date WHERE d.fiscal_year_label IN ('FY25', 'FY26') AND i.fully_paid_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) AS q GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1) AS q LIMIT 500

results.question: How did the channel overstock rate over the 13 weeks from Monday 30 March to Sunday 28 June 2026 compare with the same 13 weeks of 2025, Monday 31 March to Sunday 29 June 2025?
results.answer_text: The overstock rate was 24.89% of distributor-SKU-days in the 13 weeks to 28 June 2026, against 23.94% in the same 13 weeks of 2025. That is about 0.96 percentage points higher. results.question: Why did base-crack warranty claims rise at our Durgapur plant in 2025?
results.answer_text: Durgapur base-crack claims rose from about 45 a month in Jan–Feb 2025 to a peak of 74 in June 2025, and stayed at 54–67 a month for the rest of the year. A large part of the rise traces to one resin lot, RL-DGP-L2-250310 on Line 2. It was used in March–April 2025 production and accounts for 197 of the 695 base-crack claims in 2025 (498 came from other lots). Those lots also show older Line 2 lots with elevated claims. This points to a resin-lot/Line 2 cause, but I haven't normalised claims by units shipped, so treat it as a lead for QA to investigate, not proof. No defined metric covered this, so the figures come from ad hoc SQL.

results.question: As of 23 September 2026, which distributor shows the clearest channel stress, with sell-out falling while sell-in holds up, and what is behind it?
results.answer_text: No defined metric covered this, so the result comes from ad hoc SQL on the weekly distributor health mart (week of 14 Sep 2026, snapshot 20 Sep). D0046 (South Bengal) shows the clearest stress. Its 8-week sell-out is only 0.141 of last year's level, while 12-week sell-in is 3.17 times sell-out. The cause is stock build-up: it holds about 255 days of stock, 2.18 times the median distributor. Payment is not the issue (DSO 29.6 days, below median) and a rep visit was verified 3 days ago. It has no scheme invoices, so scheme stuffing doesn't explain it. D0253, D0246 and D0204 also have steep sell-out declines, but their sell-in to sell-out ratios are lower.

results.question: Which district has the most installer-attributed warranty claims, and why are claims there so high? Is a bad production batch to blame?
results.answer_text: Kamrup Metropolitan has the most installer-attributed warranty claims (602), ahead of Kolkata (373) and Patna (330). A bad batch doesn't look like the cause. Those claims come from 500 different batches, and no batch has more than 4 claims there. One installer does stand out: INS0227 (Sunita Mondal) has 140 claims, or 9.4 per 1,000 units installed. The other top installers there are at about 3.5–4.2 per 1,000. This points to installer practice rather than production, but the data doesn't prove the cause. No defined metric covered this, so the results come from ad hoc SQL.

results.question: Why does channel stock tend to rise right after each quarter-end?
results.answer_text: The data points to quarter-end primary loading, but it doesn't prove cause. No defined metric covered this, so I used an ad hoc query. In March each year, shipments to distributors spike above retailer sales. For example, March 2025 primary was about 2.09M units against about 1.78M secondary, with about 236K units on scheme invoices. Average channel stock then climbs in April, from about 2.54M to about 2.80M units. The same pattern holds in 2024 and 2026. The June and September quarter-ends show smaller scheme volumes and no comparable stock jump.

results.question: Warranty claim costs were higher in FY26 than in FY25. What drove the increase?
results.answer_text: Total warranty claim cost rose from about ₹23.5M in FY25 to about ₹29.5M in FY26, an increase of about ₹5.95M. Base-crack claims drove most of it. Their cost went from about ₹19.3M to ₹24.9M, which is ₹5.54M of the increase. Base-crack claims rose from 2,243 to 2,805. Other failure modes rose only slightly, from about ₹4.2M to ₹4.6M combined. Average cost per claim also rose, from about ₹4,024 to ₹4,317. No governed metric covered this, so I used ad-hoc SQL on the claims data. All claims are tanks, and all three plants rose broadly in step.

results.question: As of 23 September 2026, which distributor owes us the most overdue money, and why has it built up?
results.answer_text: As of 23 Sep 2026, D0219 (Pritam Debbarma Enterprises, Odisha, Tier 1) has the most overdue money: about ₹3.34M across 2 invoices, 4 to 11 days past due. The build-up comes from a few large weekly invoices that haven't been paid. D0219 has paid nothing on any of its 6 open invoices, and the largest overdue one is INV0034589 at about ₹2.57M. None of the invoices are scheme-related. Its credit limit is ₹29M and it is active, so the data points to slow payment on recent large invoices, not a long-standing arrears problem. No defined metric covered this, so I used ad hoc SQL.

results.question: Sell-out in Assam jumped in Q1 FY27 (April to June 2026) compared with Q1 FY26. Which distributor drove most of that growth, and what was behind it?
results.answer_text: New Biswas Traders (D0118, Kamrup Metropolitan) drove the most growth. Its sell-out rose from ₹24.3M to ₹30.6M, up about ₹6.3M, which is roughly 35% of Assam's net growth of ₹17.7M across distributors. The growth was broad, covering all four categories. Fittings volume rose from 35,084 to 58,650 units and pipes from 20,083 to 26,832 units. Tanks and sanitaryware also grew, and the number of retailers buying fittings rose from 21 to 27. The distributor's primary purchases rose from ₹18.4M to ₹28.7M, and all 28 scheme-invoice lines fall in Q1 FY27 (none in Q1 FY26). That points to a scheme, but I haven't tested it. No defined metric covered this, so these figures come from ad hoc SQL.

results.question: Which distributor had the weakest health score in the week starting Monday 14 September 2026, and what is dragging it down?
results.answer_text: Distributor D0128 (Assam) had the weakest health score for the week of 14 Sep 2026, at 4.5. This came from an ad-hoc query because no defined metric covered it. Two of its component scores were 0: secondary sales trend (8-week secondary units were only 0.265 of last year's) and DSO trend (DSO 1.25x the median). Days of stock was 2.4x the median, which scored 6.3. The primary-to-secondary gap also scored 6.3. Visit recency was its best component at 22.9, with the last verified visit 18 days earlier. The next weakest were D0037 at 5.7 and D0253 at 7.7.

results.question: Which distributor looks most like it is being loaded with stock at quarter-end, and what is the evidence?
results.answer_text: No defined metric covered this, so I used ad-hoc SQL on the scheme-quarter stuffing flags. The strongest single case is D0202 (Bihar & Jharkhand, tier 2) in FY25Q1. In the scheme window its pipe units ran at 2.45x its baseline rate (1,992 vs 4,874 baseline units, window concentration 1.27). Its tank units ran at 2.43x. Sell-through then stopped (post-window rate ratio 0.0), and days of stock stayed about 255 (pipes) and 283 (tanks) above the pre-window level 60 days later. If you mean the most repeated pattern instead, D0092, D0235 and D0311 each have 11 confirmed stuffing quarters.

results.question: Which installer has the most unusual warranty claim rate, and is that a product problem or an installation problem?
results.answer_text: No defined metric covered this, so I used ad hoc SQL. Installer Sunita Mondal (INS0227, certified, Kamrup Metropolitan) has the most unusual claim rate: 140 claims on 14,863 units, or 9.4 per 1,000. That is about 6.3 standard deviations above the mean of installers with at least 50 units. The next highest is 6.3 per 1,000. Her claims are spread across 55 batches, 23 resin lots, both plants and all failure modes, with no batch having more than 2 of her claims. That points to an installation or site issue rather than a product defect, though this is indicative and not proof.

results.question: Which region had the most distributors at risk in the week starting Monday 14 September 2026, and what is behind it?
results.answer_text: South Bengal had the most at-risk distributors in the week of 14 Sep 2026, with 2 (D0037 and D0080). Odisha had 1 (D0204) and no other region had any. In South Bengal, both distributors show secondary sales running well below last year (8-week trend ratios of 0.22 and 0.67) and very high days of stock (406 and 127). D0037 also has a primary-to-secondary gap, and D0080 has a high DSO score. Neither has had a verified visit in 12 or more days. No defined metric covered this, so these figures come from ad hoc SQL.

results.question: Sell-in to distributors jumps in the last weeks of each quarter. Is that real demand, or something else?
results.answer_text: Much of it looks like scheme-driven channel stuffing, not real demand. Across FY24Q4–FY27Q1, about half or more of the quarter-end window units came from scheme invoices. For example, FY26Q4 had 266,819 scheme units out of 490,136 window units. In every quarter, 100–200 distributor-quarters were flagged for stuffing, and in most quarters a large share were confirmed by a drop in sell-in after the window. Excess days of stock stayed positive in most quarters. This is based on the scheme-quarter mart, and no defined metric covered it directly. I did not compare it with secondary (retail) sales here.
results.confidence_note: 3/4 figures traced to query results; untraced: 100.

results.question: What is driving warranty claim costs at the Durgapur plant in FY26?
results.answer_text: Base-crack failures drive Durgapur's FY26 warranty cost. They account for about ₹6.74M of the ₹7.74M total, or 87%, from 755 of 1,618 claims. All of those base-crack claims trace to production line 2. The cost is concentrated in tank SKUs: GP-TNK-1000-3L is 36% of base-crack cost and GP-TNK-2000-3L is 24%. Leak (5.7%) and fitting failure (4.0%) are minor. No defined metric covered this, so I used ad-hoc SQL on claims dated in FY26, assigned to the plant through the claim's batch.

results.question: How is sell-in this year comparing with last year so far?
results.answer_text: Sell-in (primary sales value) is up about 8% on last year over the same period, through 23 Sep 2026. No defined metric covered this, so I used ad hoc SQL. On a fiscal-year basis (from 1 Apr), it is ₹2.26bn against ₹2.08bn, up 8.5%. On a calendar-year basis (from 1 Jan), it is ₹3.62bn against ₹3.35bn, up 8.1%.
